import json

# Build the output grid based on the pattern
# Pattern: for each special cell (value 1), draw diagonals with slope +1 and -1
# Both main diagonals extending in all 4 directions

# Test input has 1s at these positions (row, col)
positions_1 = [
    (2, 2),   # row 2, col 2
    (4, 14),  # row 4, col 14
    (10, 10), # row 10, col 10
    (18, 9),  # row 18, col 9
]

grid = [[4 for c in range(16)] for r in range(19)]

# Mark all cells on diagonals from each position
for row, col in positions_1:
    # All 4 diagonal directions: (+1,+1), (+1,-1), (-1,+1), (-1,-1)
    # Start from original position and move outwards
    r, c = row, col
    
    # Direction (+1, +1) - down-right
    while True:
        if r >= 19 or c >= 16: break
        grid[r][c] = 1
        r += 1
        c += 1
    
    r, c = row, col
    # Direction (+1, -1) - down-left
    while True:
        if r >= 19 or c < 0: break
        grid[r][c] = 1
        r += 1
        c -= 1
    
    r, c = row, col
    # Direction (-1, +1) - up-right
    while True:
        if r < 0 or c >= 16: break
        grid[r][c] = 1
        r -= 1
        c += 1
    
    r, c = row, col
    # Direction (-1, -1) - up-left
    while True:
        if r < 0 or c < 0: break
        grid[r][c] = 1
        r -= 1
        c -= 1

# Convert to list of lists for submission
output = [row[:] for row in grid]
print(json.dumps(output))

import json

# Demo analysis:
# Input 1s at: (2,1) and (7,6)
# Output has diagonal from (2,1) to (7,6) with slope +1
# Pattern: for each pair of special cells, draw all 4 diagonal lines connecting them

# For the test input, I need to find all 1 positions:
# Row 2: col 2 -> (2,2)
# Row 4: cols 4 and 14 -> (4,4) and (4,14)
# Row 6: col 6 -> (6,6)
# Row 7: col 14 -> (7,14)
# Row 10: col 10 -> (10,10)
# Row 15: col 2 -> (15,2)
# Row 18: col 9 -> (18,9)

positions_1 = [
    (2, 2),
    (4, 4),
    (4, 14),
    (6, 6),
    (7, 14),
    (10, 10),
    (15, 2),
    (18, 9),
]

grid = [[4 for c in range(16)] for r in range(19)]

# Draw all 4 diagonal lines between every pair of points
def get_diag_cells(p1, p2):
    """Get all cells on diagonals passing through p1 and p2"""
    # Check if they're on the same diagonal (slope +1 or -1)
    dr = p2[0] - p1[0]
    dc = p2[1] - p1[1]
    
    # Same diagonal if |dr| == |dc|
    if abs(dr) != abs(dc):
        return set()
    
    result = set()
    r1, c1 = p1
    r2, c2 = p2
    
    step_r = 1 if dr > 0 else (-1 if dr < 0 else 0)
    step_c = 1 if dc > 0 else (-1 if dc < 0 else 0)
    
    # Draw line from p1 to p2
    curr_r, curr_c = r1, c1
    while True:
        result.add((curr_r, curr_c))
        if (curr_r, curr_c) == (r2, c2):
            break
        curr_r += step_r
        curr_c += step_c
    
    return result

# Generate all diagonal connections
for i in range(len(positions_1)):
    for j in range(i + 1, len(positions_1)):
        diag_cells = get_diag_cells(positions_1[i], positions_1[j])
        for r, c in diag_cells:
            grid[r][c] = 1

output = [row[:] for row in grid]
print(json.dumps(output))
